title: The so-called clique and pride in hits
summary: He says the studio group became a clique only because producers asked for the players on earlier hits, and discusses guessing hits.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So speaking of people, people, why do you think this clique, why do you think this group continued to get quote-unquote most of the session work? I mean, what was the, beyond their musical ability? I mean, beyond their musical ability.

I think that when Cosmo called us and we started doing these things and people were saying, hey, man, they sound good together. Now people say, man, you guys had a clique. It wasn't by, by us saying that we don't want to play with anybody else. Yeah. It was just that the people that would come in, the independents would come in and say, we want the guys that played on such and such an album. Oh,
Or such and such record, really. Mm-hmm. So, they would call for us. Right. And Cosmo would get in touch with us.
Yeah, I want that drummer, I want that saxophone player.

Yeah. The guys that did such and such a thing. Who are those guys that said, well, I can get in touch with them. Mm-hmm. And so people said, we had a clique. Mm-hmm. And probably it was, but it wasn't our doing. Mm-hmm. It wasn't like we said, well, we're going to shut everybody else out because we're going to be the ones. You know, it was somebody who said, we want them. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
So, did you, did you, so did you become conscious of the records that you played on and, well, this one's in the charts or this one's making this noise?

Oh, we were quite proud of something. If we did it and it went up in the charts, you know, we would say, hey, man, we would have such a thing, you know, but at the time we were doing it, we didn't think much of it because a lot of times when we thought a record was going to be outstanding, the public didn't much care for it, so we weren't always right. Sometimes we say, this is going to be a hit and it was.
